digo: Chikombe tsui; Chinyakore (northern Digo; Chinyakole in the south)
other_mijikenda: Swahili: shares the name chikombe tsui (Pakia App. VI)

teaser.en: Hooked thorns that grab like a leopard's claws: Digo named this scrambling acacia for exactly that.
teaser.sw: Miiba iliyopinda kama ndoano inayonasa kama makucha ya chui: Wadigo waliupa mgunga huu unaotambaa jina kwa sababu hiyo hasa.

summary.en: *Chikombe tsui*, 'leopard's claws', is a scrambling, prickly acacia of the coastal bush. Digo give the same name to a thorny caper bush because the two share the same claw-like thorns.
summary.sw: *Chikombe tsui*, 'makucha ya chui', ni mgunga unaotambaa wenye miiba, wa vichaka vya pwani. Wadigo hukipa kichaka cha jamii ya caper chenye miiba jina hilo hilo kwa sababu vyote viwili vina miiba ile ile kama makucha.

about.en: *Acacia adenocalyx* (now *Senegalia adenocalyx*) is a climbing or scrambling shrub armed with small, sharply hooked prickles that catch on skin and clothing. Like other acacias it has feathery, twice-divided leaves, small flowers in spikes or heads, and flat pods. Digo identify it by its leaves.
about.sw: *Acacia adenocalyx* (sasa *Senegalia adenocalyx*) ni kichaka kinachopanda au kutambaa, kilichojaa miiba midogo iliyopinda kama ndoano kwa ukali, inayonasa ngozi na nguo. Kama migunga mingine, kina majani yaliyo kama manyoya yaliyogawanyika mara mbili, maua madogo katika vishada virefu au vichwa, na maganda bapa. Wadigo hukitambua kwa majani yake.

where.en: It grows in coastal bush and thicket in Kenya, Tanzania and Mozambique.
where.sw: Huota katika vichaka na vichaka vizito vya pwani nchini Kenya, Tanzania na Msumbiji.

culture.en: Pakia uses *chikombe tsui* as an example of how Digo group plants. A single folk name covers two quite different plants, this acacia and the caper bush *Capparis viminea*, because both have the same claw-like thorns. Unlike plants grouped because they share a use, the two are not used in the same way. Digo also put it among the *miya*, their general category for thorny plants.
culture.sw: Pakia anatumia *chikombe tsui* kama mfano wa jinsi Wadigo wanavyopanga mimea katika makundi. Jina moja la kienyeji linajumuisha mimea miwili tofauti kabisa, mgunga huu na kichaka cha jamii ya caper *Capparis viminea*, kwa sababu yote miwili ina miiba ile ile kama makucha. Tofauti na mimea inayowekwa pamoja kwa sababu ya matumizi yanayofanana, mimea hii miwili haitumiki kwa njia moja. Wadigo pia huuweka miongoni mwa *miya*, kundi lao la jumla la mimea yenye miiba.

names.en: *Chikombe tsui* means 'claws of a leopard': its thorns are likened to the claws (*kombe*) of a leopard (*tsui*). The name is shared with Swahili. Pakia also records *chinyakore*, pronounced *chinyakole* by southern Digo, as an example of how names differ between northern and southern Digo. One passage in his text links *chikombe tsui* to *Acacia mellifera*, a different tree that the existing reference calls *chikwata kombe*.
names.sw: *Chikombe tsui* maana yake ni 'makucha ya chui': miiba yake inafananishwa na makucha (*kombe*) ya chui (*tsui*). Jina hili linashirikiwa na Kiswahili. Pakia pia ameandika *chinyakore*, linalotamkwa *chinyakole* na Wadigo wa kusini, kama mfano wa jinsi majina yanavyotofautiana kati ya Wadigo wa kaskazini na wa kusini. Kifungu kimoja katika maandishi yake kinahusisha *chikombe tsui* na *Acacia mellifera*, mti tofauti ambao marejeo yaliyopo yanauita *chikwata kombe*.
